messages:
mia.cs: Quick ask — can we spin up a one-page 'Edge Priming cooklet' for customers: short checklist + dos/don'ts for caching, batching, streaming they can hand to their SREs? Need something <1 page for field handoff, preferably non‑technical language they can forward. Can someone draft in the next 24h?

sam.se: Yep, I can take a pass. Goal: short bullets, an optional one‑paragraph explainer, and a tiny code sample for engineering. Focus on three scenarios: interactive UI, background batch jobs, bursty onboarding traffic.

anita_csm: Add a renewal-risk cue: if post-launch active sessions drop >40% in 48h, flag renewal team and run a 1:1. Also remind customers that aggressive prefill increases immediate token usage — call it out under costs.

jorge.eng: +1. I'll add a practical snippet for prefill / warm pools. Keep it tiny so customers' SREs can paste into a runbook: 

jorge.eng: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "X-Redwood-Priming: tenant-42" \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd-2-small","prefill_tokens":1500,"ttl_seconds":300,"strategy":"kv-prefix"}'
```

jorge.eng: Suggested tunables (engineering-facing, put in an appendix): batching_window_ms=25, max_batch_size=32, cache_ttl_s=300, kv_cache_enabled=true, streaming_chunk_ms=50. Note: reduce batch window to 10–15ms for super-low-latency widgets.

ellie.pm: For the customer note: keep one sentence per idea. Example lines: 
- "Start with a small warm pool (5–10 prefills) 5 minutes before your expected peak."
- "Use short cache TTLs (3–10 minutes) for personalized sessions; longer TTLs (10–60 minutes) are OK for shared system prompts."
- "If you need single-digit latency for interactive UI, disable large batch windows and prefer small batches or streaming."

sam.se: Draft TL;DR bullets to paste into an onboarding email (customer-facing):
- Keep it short: "Edge Priming Quick Guide — 4 actions to reduce cold latency"
- Action 1: "Prefill a tiny warm pool (5–10 requests) ~5 minutes before launch; TTL ~5m."
- Action 2: "Batch background jobs (batch window ~20–50ms, max 16–32) to save cost without hurting UX."
- Action 3: "Use short per-tenant cache TTLs for personalization; use longer shared caches for static system prompts."
- Action 4: "Enable streaming for interactive flows — set chunk latency ~30–60ms to balance throughput and perceived latency."
- Quick cost note: "Prefilling uses tokens up front; scale warm pools conservatively and monitor usage metrics."

mia.cs: This is great. Can we also include two quick troubleshooting lines for the customer: 
1) "If you see sudden drop in request rate post-go-live, check client-side retries and token limits."
2) "If latency spikes >200ms for >5% of requests, open a ticket and include a sample request id."

anita_csm: Add the renewal ops flag as a single line the CS rep can click: 
- "If 48h activation <60% of expected, tag @renewals and schedule a re-onboard call."

ops-bot: Note: Remember to run /reserve-warm-pool tenant-42 before major demos — automation helps.

sam.se: I'll stitch this into a one‑page layout and drop a Doc link. Keep the doc shareable (customer view) and include the curl snippet in an engineering appendix.

mia.cs: Perfect. I'll proof and send to the onboarding folder and paste the one‑page into the Welcome email. Will ping you all before sending. :rocket:
